contentHtml:
Packing for a trip to the jungle of San Luis Potosí means putting together clothes, shoes and gear designed to get around safely among waterfalls, rivers and tropical forest. Packing well before you leave is the difference between making the most of every attraction and staying on the riverbank because you forgot the basics. The Huasteca Potosina combines heat, intense humidity, slippery ground and lots of water, so it pays to pack with care.

In this article you'll find a detailed checklist with everything you need for your trip to Xilitla and the rest of the region: from water shoes to the right insect repellent. According to local operators in the region, more than 70% of travelers who arrive without the right footwear in 2026 have to skip at least one water activity for safety reasons.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and tour operators in the region. This guide is updated with the real experiences of people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: October 2026. Before you pack, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina so you know exactly how many days and which activities you need to pack for.

What to pack for the Huasteca Potosina: the essentials

Which water shoes work best for the waterfalls?

Water shoes with non-slip rubber soles are a must in the Huasteca Potosina. The rocks in the rivers and pools are covered in moss and extremely slippery. In 2026, getting to Tamul Waterfall by shared boat costs between $150 and $250 MXN per person, and part of the trip involves walking along the riverbank over bare rock.

Amphibious-style water shoes—with a heel strap and fast-draining soles—are the most practical choice. Open sandals without a strap are easily lost in the current and don't give you enough grip. Book your tour and arrive with the right shoes ready to go.

Insect repellent: the item most often forgotten

Repellent with 30% DEET or higher is essential at any time of year, but especially between May and October, when mosquito and gnat activity peaks. Put it on before you leave your hotel, not just when you reach the sights, because the bugs also live along the trails and in the shady areas under the trees.

Choose a stick or lotion repellent instead of a spray so the wind doesn't blow it away before it sticks to your skin. If you're traveling with kids, ask your pediatrician about a formula that's right for children. You can read more about activities for the whole family in our 2026 guide to the Huasteca Potosina with kids.

A complete packing list for your trip to Xilitla and the waterfall route

What travelers who pack well have to say

People who arrive in Xilitla with the right gear enjoy Edward James's Las Pozas without a hitch: admission in 2026 is $180 MXN per adult, paid at the garden's ticket window, and the visit involves climbing wet steps and walking on uneven surfaces. Sturdy shoes and quick-dry clothes completely change the experience.

Carry an extra change of clothes in a zip-top bag inside your backpack. The jungle of San Luis Potosí can surprise you with sudden rain even in the dry season. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina

How much does a tour cost, and how should you pack for each type of tour?

Our day tours priced per person range from $900 MXN to $1,950 MXN, and our 3-day, 2-night package with a hotel in Xilitla, Huasteca Immersion (Inmersión Huasteca), costs $8,699 MXN per couple. For full-day tours, bring a small backpack of 20 liters at most, with a waterproof zipper. Check out our 3-day Huasteca Potosina guide and adjust your packing to the number of water activities you have planned.

Final checklist: tips before you zip up your suitcase

ItemWhy do you need it?Where will you use it?
Water shoes with non-slip solesWet rocks and surfaces at waterfalls and poolsTamul, Micos, Tamasopo, Xilitla
Repellent with ≥30% DEETBugs in the jungle and shady areasThe whole trip
Quick-dry clothingWater activities and humid heatAll the waterfalls
Waterproof bag for documentsSplashing on the boat and sudden rainTamul river trip
Water-resistant SPF 50+ sunscreenIntense sun exposure on open riversMicos, Tamul, Tamasopo
  • Lightweight long-sleeved clothing: It protects you from sun and bugs. Go for technical fabrics or linen; cotton takes a long time to dry.
  • A waterproof backpack or one with a rain cover: The boat rides on the Tamul river mean constant splashing. Learn more in our guide to rafting on the Tampaón River.
  • A basic first-aid kit and antihistamines: Include bandages, hand sanitizer and stomach medicine.
  • Cash in small bills: Admission fees range from $30 MXN (Sótano de las Golondrinas) to $180 MXN (Las Pozas in Xilitla, plus $30 MXN for the mandatory guide). Several places don't take cards.

Frequently asked questions about packing

What footwear is required to visit the waterfalls of the Huasteca Potosina?

Water shoes with non-slip soles are a must at waterfalls like Micos and Tamasopo and on the way to Tamul. Open sandals don't give you the grip you need on wet rocks. In 2026, several access points require walking directly over rock with water running across it.

How much cash should I bring for admission fees and tours?

Bring at least $500 MXN in cash per day for individual admission fees: Micos costs $80–$100 MXN, Las Pozas in Xilitla $180 MXN per adult and the boat to Tamul between $150 and $250 MXN. Agency packages include several admission fees.

When is the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina with less rain?

The best season is November to April, when the weather is drier and milder. In those months the waterfalls keep a good flow without the dangerous summer floods. Find more details in our guide to the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina.

Is Xilitla safe for a family trip, and which repellent do you recommend?

A trip to Xilitla is safe for families if you follow basic precautions. Bring repellent with 30% DEET for adults and look for a DEET-free formula for children under 12. Travel during the day when possible, and hire certified local guides for jungle outings.
